title: Assent, consent, and legal enforceability
summary: Shared understanding, voluntary participation, and the significance of legal commitment are related but distinct.
notes: The chapter opens by distinguishing assent to an exchange, consent involving capacity and absence of impermissible coercion, and the role of an intention concerning legal enforcement. A coercive exchange can be understood by both parties and still lack the necessary voluntary consent. Restatement § 21 does not generally require an affirmative intention to incur legal obligation, but manifested intention not to be legally bound can matter. The editors note that courts sometimes use “mutual assent” to encompass more than one of these issues.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 169–173. Open assigned page 169.
